entries.complaint: "ISO" almost universally means the International Organization for Standardization to a Portuguese technical reader, not the (US) Insurance Services Office this string means. The English spells out "Insurance Services Office (ISO)" so an English reader is warned, but a Portuguese sentence carrying the same acronym still risks being read as an ISO standard reference (e.g. an ISO 24510-family water-utility standard) rather than a US insurance-industry fire-flow credit rule, since Portuguese has no equivalent institution the reader would recognize by that initialism.
readings: Translated literally, keeping "Insurance Services Office (ISO)" spelled out and trusting the parenthetical to disambiguate, as in English (chosen)
Add a short clarifying gloss (e.g. "entidade seguradora dos EUA") so the sentence cannot be misread as citing an ISO standard

entries.complaint: "DEM" (Digital Elevation Model) has no glossary entry for this sprint. Brazilian GIS practice commonly abbreviates the concept as "MDE" (Modelo Digital de Elevação), but the feature is also tied to a specific product name, "Mapbox DEM" (see lpn_elev_dem_said, lpn_settings_elev_source_dem), which is not something to translate. I kept the bare acronym "DEM" untranslated everywhere (Ler o DEM, Usar o DEM, DEM do Mapbox) for internal consistency with the product name, rather than switching to "MDE" for generic references and "DEM" only for the product name, which would read as two different things to a user. I am not confident this is the reading Tom intends.
readings: Keep "DEM" untranslated everywhere, treating it as tied to the Mapbox DEM product name (chosen)
Use the established Portuguese GIS abbreviation "MDE" for the generic elevation-model concept and reserve "DEM" only for the literal product name "Mapbox DEM"
